name: Rolldown
tagline: A Rust-based JavaScript and TypeScript bundler with a TypeScript API.
hook: Splits internal documentation into design rationale and implementation mechanics, and assigns CI suites by change type.
summary: Rolldown treats instructions as a route into the context missing from code. Its root guide describes a three-layer runtime, generated bindings, and the CI coverage needed for browser, Windows, and WebContainer changes.

techniques.title: Separate rationale from machinery
techniques.body: Internal documentation has distinct design and implementation files. A feature only needs a design file when there is reasoning worth retaining, so the structure does not require inventing rationale for every feature.
techniques.quote: A feature with no recorded rationale keeps only `implementation.md`; add `design.md` when there's a _why_ worth capturing.

techniques.title: Remove context that code now explains
techniques.body: The guide asks maintainers to trim completed details while retaining decisions, failure modes, and unresolved questions. Documentation is maintained for the context it adds, not for a complete inventory of implementation.
techniques.quote: Trim what's been implemented and is now obvious from the code. Keep what's still valuable — the "why" behind decisions, failure modes, unresolved questions.

techniques.title: Specify what CI activation actually requires
techniques.body: The Windows rule requires both a label and rerunning jobs on the current PR commit. It explains why adding the label alone is insufficient.
techniques.quote: Adding the label alone does not start a workflow.

techniques.title: Distinguish execution tests from package installation tests
techniques.body: The WebContainer guidance separates the default wasm suite from a suite that installs and builds packed artifacts. Changes to bindings and their packaging therefore need an additional kind of evidence.
techniques.quote: Pure wasm behavior changes don't need it — the default CI's `wasi` job already runs the test suite against the wasm binding; this label checks that the packed packages install and work inside WebContainer.

techniques.title: Explain an internal compatibility exception
techniques.body: The root tips state that the internal Rust crates do not promise semver stability. Reviews should check in-repository callers rather than report a public compatibility violation that the project does not claim.
techniques.quote: Breaking API changes are expected and acceptable in any version — do not raise them as code-review findings as long as in-repo callers are updated.

steal: Separate design decisions from implementation descriptions.
Remove documentation that no longer adds context beyond the code.
Explain how optional CI coverage is activated.
Distinguish runtime behavior from packaged-installation behavior.
